query: How can support teams reduce ticket resolution time?

per_column.name: request_type
per_column.rationale: Categorizes tickets into request types, a clear grouping axis for comparing resolution time. Values match source text well (billing, bug, incident, feature).

per_column.name: issue_category
per_column.rationale: Domain categorization gives strong new axis to segment resolution time by problem area. Samples are sound readings of the text.

per_column.name: operational_severity
per_column.rationale: Severity is highly relevant to resolution time analysis. Mostly grounded, but CS-0001 (invoice correction) labelled 'blocked_workflow' is a stretch; some inference beyond text.

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope of impact is a genuine modeling axis. Mostly well-grounded; CS-0005 marked 'entire_tenant' is an overreach since text says only their pipeline.

per_column.name: technical_complexity
per_column.rationale: A 1-5 complexity ordinal is useful for correlating with resolution time. However the specific numeric levels are subjective inferences the text does not directly warrant, lowering groundedness.

per_column.name: escalation_signal
per_column.rationale: Escalation pressure plausibly drives prioritization and resolution speed. CS-0003 labelled 'executive_or_audit_visibility' from 'board presentation' is a reasonable inference, but CS-0004 'deadline_or_time_pressure' from a soft renewal mention is weak.

per_column.name: root_cause_domain
per_column.rationale: Root cause grouping is useful for targeting reductions. But CS-0001 (duplicate invoice line) labelled 'regression_from_release' is unsupported invention; text gives no release cause.

per_column.name: workaround_available
per_column.rationale: Workaround presence relates to urgency and resolution effort. Values largely reasonable; CS-0001 'no_workaround' is a plausible reading and CS-0005 'partial_workaround' matches the manual sed step.

per_column.name: repro_reliability
per_column.rationale: Reproducibility affects diagnosis time, a valid axis. But 'always_reproducible' asserted for CS-0001 billing issue lacks textual support; often inferred beyond evidence.

per_column.name: actionability
per_column.rationale: The type of action needed maps well onto resolution effort/time. Values are mostly defensible readings; CS-0005 'hotfix_or_rollback_needed' is sound given the release regression.

per_column.name: requires_external_dependency
per_column.rationale: External dependencies are a strong driver of delays, highly relevant. CS-0002 'customer_it_or_idp' is well-grounded, but 'internal_engineering_escalation' for CS-0001 is an assumption.

per_column.name: data_or_info_provided
per_column.rationale: Information completeness at intake plausibly affects resolution time. Values align with text (repro steps present in CS-0002/0005, minimal info in CS-0001/0003).

judge.rationale: The added columns provide a rich, largely non-redundant set of analytical axes (severity, scope, complexity, escalation, root cause, dependencies, info completeness) that are genuinely useful for modeling and reducing resolution time, directly serving the query. Groundedness is generally good with sensible 'not_present'/'not_applicable' handling for silent rows, but several columns show confident inferences unsupported by the text -- notably 'regression_from_release' as a default root cause, subjective 'technical_complexity' numerics, and 'always_reproducible' applied to non-technical tickets. These hallucinations moderate the overall groundedness score.
